summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, and chronic heart failure, was admitted due to an episode of hypotension with generalized weakness. He had inadvertently restarted spironolactone and furosemide contrary to prior discharge instructions, leading to low blood pressure. Upon evaluation, his cardiac enzymes were negative, ECG and chest X-ray were unremarkable, and no acute cardiac or pulmonary issues were found. His symptoms resolved with discontinuation of the diuretics. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout the stay, with blood pressure in the 110s to 130s. Medication adjustments were made, including holding furosemide and spironolactone until cardiology follow-up, reducing atorvastatin and metoprolol doses, and continuing all other chronic therapies. He was discharged home with clear instructions on medication management, diet, weight monitoring, and urgent follow-up.
